reference: There is no GNU/POSIX rtspcat client to serve as an equivalent CLI oracle. The runnable cases are Bash metadata contract checks: the Bash type/help builtins define their output shape, and the documented rtspcat synopsis/description supply the expected text. Protocol behavior is deferred to a future disposable VM with a scripted loopback RTSP peer and independently constructed wire/frame expectations; no network fixture is executed here.
coverage: Bash reports rtspcat as a builtin without invoking it.
Bash help exposes the documented one-line description and synopsis.

Future protocol fixture requirements cover RTSP handshake and H.264 output framing, RTP aggregation/fragmentation and access-unit boundaries, authentication/session/keepalive behavior, error handling, and output descriptor lifecycle.
exclusions: No matching GNU/POSIX rtspcat CLI exists, so no synthetic parity oracle is claimed.
No rtspcat operation was invoked: it requires an RTSP peer and network activity is out of scope. All operation cases are DEFERRED, not passes.
No unrelated loadables or external file utilities are exercised; these cases require no fixture files.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must identify the registered rtspcat command as a builtin; this checks availability metadata without entering the client operation.
Bash help -d renders the registered short description. The expected text is the documented rtspcat description, not output sampled from the candidate.
cases.stdout: rtspcat - RTSP/RTP H.264 client: access units out as framed records.

cases.purpose: Bash help -s exposes the documented command synopsis, including its supported options, without invoking rtspcat.
cases.stdout: rtspcat: rtspcat URL [-o FD] [-n COUNT] [-k SECS] [-t SECS] [-v]

cases.purpose: Exercise the client handshake, SDP track selection, TCP interleaving, one complete IDR access unit, framed stdout, and session teardown.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a scripted loopback RTSP server that accepts only the fixture connection and emits deterministic OPTIONS/DESCRIBE/SETUP/PLAY responses plus a bounded interleaved RTP stream. Validate the 4-byte big-endian length and Annex-B bytes against an independently assembled expected frame, and record request order/session teardown. No peer or network activity is run by this suite.

cases.purpose: Cover single-NAL, STAP-A and FU-A payloads, marker and timestamp access-unit boundaries, parameter-set insertion, and the requested unit limit.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM and deterministic loopback RTSP/RTP mock capable of sending explicitly numbered packet sequences. Construct expected Annex-B access units independently from the fixture NAL bytes; check each record boundary, SPS/PPS insertion before IDR, and exact -n stopping behavior.

cases.purpose: Check Basic and MD5 Digest challenges, session headers, CSeq progression, and GET_PARAMETER keepalive behavior.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a scripted loopback RTSP peer and synthetic fixture-only credentials. Independently calculate Basic encoding and RFC 1321/RFC Digest response values, then inspect request headers and keepalive exchange. No installed credentials or network targets are used here.

cases.purpose: Check malformed RTSP lengths/headers, malformed or incomplete RTP, EOF, timeout, and invalid argument handling, including that incomplete units are not emitted.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a bounded loopback protocol mock that can emit one controlled fault per run and enforce a short deadline. Expected statuses, empty/partial output rules, and valid recovery frames must be specified from RTSP/RTP framing rules and the documented CLI contract. This case was not executed.

cases.purpose: Check -o descriptor output, write failures, closed-pipe handling, and that repeated calls leave the invoking shell usable.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with the loopback RTSP mock plus private fixture files and a controlled pipe reader/closed writer. Compare successful descriptor bytes with the independently assembled frame and verify failure status and shell survival after a closed-pipe write. No external device, host path, or signal is used by this suite.
